186378:
Senator Nangle, Representative Crafts, and Members of the Transportation Committee:
Because TrainRiders Northeast did not testify at the public hearing on LD 472, Resolve, Directing the Maine-Canadian Legislative Advisory Commission and the New England and Eastern Canada Legislative Commission to Examine Restoring Passenger Rail from Boston to Montreal and cannot attend today's work session on that bill, this email is to inform you that TrainRiders does support its passage. Since 1989, one of TrainRiders' stated goals has been, and continues to be, the return of passenger rail service to various Canadian provinces, including a route from Portland to Montreal. As far back as 1999, Maine applied for and later received a designation of the rail line between Portland and Lewiston as a high-speed rail corridor from the Federal Railroad Administration as part of a route for service that might eventually extend to Montreal. Finally, an August 2011 MDOT study concluded that rail service between Portland and Montreal would attract over 200,000 passengers per year. This all shows that there is a firm basis for examining such a service from Boston, through Portland, and on to Montreal in light of current conditions and interest in passenger rail.
Thankyou. F. Bruce Sleeper, President TrainRiders Northeast

LD 472
Hello,
I hope that using this email means that this message will be shared with the transportation
committee. I am writing to say that I support both of the rail bills that are coming before the
committee today. Both of these actions support Maine's climate action plan and would be economic benefits to the state of Maine.
I live and work in Maine and do not own a car. I use the Downeaster frequently for work to meet with
work colleagues at other offices in Massachusetts and take other trains for meetings further south.
However, when I want to meet with folks in Maine, other than Portland, I have to rent or borrow a car to get there. I also have friends and family in the Lewiston area who I'm not able to see often again
due to a lack of public transportation.
Extending the train to Bangor and providing regular service to interior Maine would share the economic benefits that southern Maine has received from the Downeaster to other areas of the
state. It would also provide ways for seniors who need to see medical specialists in Southern Maine a way to get there more easily. My mother is the volunteer coordinator for Age Friendly Biddeford
and is often called to see about helping to get patients from the Bangor area to specialists in Portland. Rides have to be cobbled together from multiple agencies and if it can't be done that person has to forgo care. Having this option would allow people increased mobility and dignity.
As to extending the train to Montreal from Boston YES PLEASE. I am attending a conference in Montreal in a few weeks and very much wanted to take the train but it would require two days of travel as I'd have to go to New York first. Despite the length of the trip it's emissions would still be
less than if I flew. Flying is not only bad for the environment, it's physically uncomfortable for many
people, myself included. Having an option to get to Montreal in a day would be amazing.
Please support both of these bills.
Thank you, Ioie Grandbois 338 Main Street Biddeford, Maine

March 6, 2025
Good morning Senator Nangle, Representative Crafts, and the other distinguished members of the Joint
Standing Committee on Transportation. My name is Peggy Rotundo, and I have the privilege of representing the City of Lewiston in Senate District 21. I am here today to introduce LD 472 "Resolve
Directing the Maine Canadian Legislative Advisorv Commission and the New England and Eastern
Canada Legislative Commission to Examine Restoring Passenger Rail from Boston to Montreal."
With renewed interest in passenger rail running from Boston, through Maine to the Province of Quebec, the Legislature has an opportunity to be a part of this conversation. Possible routes from Boston to
Montreal, Quebec, Canada, have been studied by several New England states. One route would utilize the
St. Lawrence and Atlantic railroad that runs from Auburn to Quebec Province, where it would then link with the Canadian National railroad, tenninating in Montreal. This route would be ideal for overnight "sleeper" trains, where the journey is part of the vacation experience, and would bolster the tourism
industry in the state.
The planning for this undertaking would require multiple parties to be involved, including those from other states and from Canada. Given this fact, I believe the Maine-Canadian Legislative Advisory Commission would be best suited to conduct this study. Rather than a propensity study, as has been done in previous years to determine the number of passengers that would utilize this service, this resolve staits with high level policy discussions that would be used as the basis for future evaluations.
It is worth noting that a bill nearly identical to the one I am presenting today was passed last session. However, appointments to the Maine-Canadian Commission were made too late, and by the time the Commission was able to meet, the reporting window had already closed.

Tourism from Canada to Maine and vice versa has been an economic driver for both sides, and this bill would lay the groundwork for increasing this economic driver in the future. Joint Standing Committee on Transportation William Weber, Sierra Club Maine March 3, 2025 Re: Testimony in Support of L.D. 472: Resolve, Directing the Maine-Canadian Legislative Advisory Commission and the New England and Eastern Canada Legislative Commission to Examine Restoring Passenger Rail from Boston to Montreal

Senator Nangle, Representative Crafts, and members of the Joint Committee on Transportation,
I am testifying on behalf of Sierra Club Maine and the Portland Climate Action Team (PCAT) in support of L.D. 472: Resolve, Directing the Maine-Canadian Legislative Advisory Commission and the New England and Eastern Canada Legislative Commission to Examine Restoring Passenger Rail from Boston to Montreal.
Founded in 1892, Sierra Club is one of our nation's oldest and largest environmental organizations representing over 22,000 supporters and members statewide. We work diligently to amplify the power of our 3.8 million members and supporters nationwide. As we seek to build a more resilient and sustainable transportation system in Maine that better connects our communities and encourages tourism, we urge you to support all efforts to expand passenger rail service, especially as it relates to expanding tourism opportunities between Maine and Canada.
We understand that since this legislation passed in the last session the Legislative Commissions were not able to meet to study this issue. The Sierra Club would strongly urge the Committee to unanimously pass this legislation as a demonstration of Maine's continued commitment to our close relationship with our friends to the north. In addition to fostering that historical relationship the Sierra Club Maine and PCAT support this study for the following substantive reasons:
1. Passenger rail service has one of the lowest emission rates compared to other forms of transportation.
2. Canadian tourism has been an important aspect of our local economy and transportation options should be supported.
This bill directs the Maine-Canadian Legislative Advisory Commission and the New England and Eastern Canada Legislative Commission to examine restoring passenger rail from Boston, Massachusetts to Montreal, Quebec, which would at the same time link the major Maine urban centers of Portland and Auburn with tourist centers that are popular with Canadiens. A map of the preliminary route is provided below.

Proposed route for a revived Grand Trunk Railroad between Montreal and Boston. Night Train Foundation
One of the main goals in the Maine State Rail Plan (1) is to support economic activity and improve Maine's quality of life through transportation investments that promote energy efficiency, environmental sustainability, and equity. A potential passenger rail link between southern Maine and Montreal would boost economic activity through improved tourism but also reduce greenhouse gas emissions from the use of private automobiles.
Senate Bill 472 includes a comprehensive assessment of the economic, social, and environmental impacts of restoring the rail line between Boston and Montreal. It must be noted that the Boston and Maine (B&M) Railroad connected Montreal to Old Orchard Beach as early as the 1850s. Because OOB is one of the closest seaside resorts to Montreal it has long experienced a strong and vibrant influence from Canada. We hope this can be encouraged in the face of imposing destructive tariffs.
The last time my wife and I visited Montreal was by car and if you have ever made that trek you know it can be tedious as well as boring. A train ride with the possibility of dinner service would be an excellent way to travel and would avoid the congestion on the roads approaching Montreal.

Reintroducing passenger rail could stimulate economic growth, improve tourism, and provide a welcome alternative to automobile road traffic. As stated earlier, the carbon footprint related to passenger rail is much less than the single use passenger auto and approximately one third the CO2 emissions resulting from flying. As railroad engines continue to convert to electricity, these traction motors will lead to a further reduction in greenhouse gas emissions. See the chart below comparing various modes of transportation.
The financial viability of the project, in whole or in part, would be examined to determine if the potential benefits outweigh the costs of restoring the rail infrastructure and maintaining it. The passenger rail service would also be compared to alternative modes such as buses and air travel. We believe given the current state of affairs between the United States and Canada, with a likely decline in the tourism industry, that this study should be given a high priority with the MDOT. If the study finds that the restored route provides positive results the project should move forward. We encourage the committee to support L.D. 472 and support passenger rail between Canada and Maine. William J Weber Sierra Club Maine Portland Climate Action Team
